title: Lets Talk Sustainable Teacher-Student Relationships
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Stuart opens by pushing back on the popular claim that school is all about relationships, insisting that school’s real purpose is advancing students’ long-term flourishing through mastery—though relationships are a critical enabler of that goal. He introduces MGCs (Moments of Genuine Connection) as a clipboard-based system for secondary teachers managing large rosters, describing the strategy as quick to explain but deep enough to spend a career refining. The article captures a tension central to Stuart’s relational framework: relationships serve learning, not the reverse, and the simplest strategies often have the most complex institutional adoption curves. The piece also notes that MGCs have demonstrated unexpected soul-deepening effects on teachers themselves, not just on student motivation.
points: Stuart explicitly rejects “school is all about relationships” as the framing for teacher work; the actual goal is student mastery and long-term flourishing, with relationships in service of that aim rather than as the aim itself.

MGCs reduce the relationship-building problem for secondary teachers to a clipboard, a printed tracking sheet, and brief intentional micro-moments that signal to each student: you are valued, known, and respected.
The strategy is easy to understand in under two minutes, yet experienced practitioners continue to refine it indefinitely—a hallmark of a strategy with genuine depth beneath its accessible surface.

Whole-school MGC adoption is significantly more complex than individual adoption, and Stuart has observed this gap grow more apparent with each school-level implementation partnership over the past two years.
quotes: I’m the last person that’s going to tell you school is all about relationships. Because it’s not. It’s all about advancing the long-term flourishing of young people by teaching them to master things that, apart from school, they’d be unlikely to master.

few factors are as critical to long-term student and teacher flourishing as good, working relationships between educators and students. And when you’re a secondary teacher working with 100+ kids… building those relationships is a tall order.

MGCs are a special kind of strategy: I can explain the what/why/how to you in just a moment or two — so simple — but here I am, thousands of MGCs into my career, and I’m still learning, tweaking, adjusting, and improving — so deep.
And in the past couple years, I’ve been blown away by how complex it is to get whole schools to adopt and gain proficiency at something so basic.
I’ll discuss how I’ve found MGCs to deepen my soul and expand my experience of the goodness of life (sounds cheesy, but it’s true).
I’ll share what works best in getting MGCs installed at the baseline “this is who we are, this is what we do” level of faculty culture.
